The test image shows a tomato leaf with distinctive **concentric ring patterns** (ring spots) across the surface — lighter green circles on darker green background, with some small dark lesions. This pattern strongly suggests a viral disease. Top candidates: **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus** and **Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus**.

Let me view one reference from each candidate, starting with my top picks.
CMV reference shows leaf distortion, not matching. Let me check more TSWV references and Early Blight.
Now let me view one reference from each remaining class systematically.

I've now used all 16 reference views. Let me summarize my analysis:

**Test image key features:**
- Green tomato leaf with prominent concentric ring/circular patterns (lighter green circles on darker green)
- Ring spots distributed across the full leaf surface
- Some small dark lesions scattered among the rings
- Leaf remains mostly intact (no severe necrosis or wilting)

**Reference review results:**
- **TSWV**: Bugwood_10 showed purple/bronze leaf spots; Bugwood_137 showed classic ring spots on pepper fruit (confirming TSWV causes this ring-spot pattern); Bugwood_162 was a field view
- **CMV**: Distorted/shoestring leaves — no match
- **Early_Blight**: Severe brown necrotic target spots — no match
- **Septoria**: Small dark-centered spots with yellowing — no match
- **Bacterial classes**: Wilting, necrotic margins, streaming tests — no match
- **Fungal classes** (Gray_Mold, Rhizopus, Late_Blight, Alternaria): Microscopic images or fruit rot — no match
- **Leaf_Mold, Powdery_Mildew**: Different symptoms (yellowing, white powder) — no match

The concentric ring spot pattern on a green, intact leaf is the defining visual hallmark of **Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus**. The TSWV pepper fruit reference confirmed this pathogen causes ring spots. No other class reviewed produces this circular ring pattern on leaf tissue.
